title: A misspelled word in a large folder lists accidental matches and drops the file that was meant
problem: Found and measured by the reviewer of 'typo-fallback-near-miss' (done record: /home/user/polish-tools/done/typo-fallback-near-miss.json, first item under 'Found, not fixed'). In `Engine::search` (crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs) the typo matches fff-search returns are a fallback: `if !settings.typos || raw.iter().any(&strict) { raw.retain(strict) } else { keep the near misses }`, where `strict` is `checked.iter().all(|w| is_subsequence(w, &hit.rel))`: every word's letters in order anywhere along the path inside the folder searched. In a tree of any size some path has the letters of a misspelled word in order by accident, scattered over its folders and its name. Then `any(strict)` is true, the fallback is never reached, the file that was meant, one typo away and returned by fff-search, is dropped as a typo match, and the accidental matches are listed. The reviewer's numbers: in the cargo registry (42,275 files) all 27 misspellings of real names tried (`carog`, `raedme`, `licnese`, `benchmrak`, `mainfest` and others) listed such matches and never reached the fallback; `benchmrak` lists two normalizer benches and no benchmark.rs. In a home-like fixture (3,065 files, long names) 123 of 169 one-typo searches for words of the tree did not reach it, and for 31 of them nothing with the intended word was listed. So the near-miss rule that 'typo-fallback-near-miss' added helps only where no path has the letters in order; in the folders people really search, a typo still gives junk. Two smaller things from the same record, in the same code: near misses are not ranked by where they are or how close (`mian` in the demo folder lists the 120 files of the folder Many, whose name has `man`, ahead of main.rs, which is row 121 of 122); and apps are found by letters in order only, so `safair` does not find Safari.
proposal: Reproduce first with engine tests on a fixture big enough to have accidental matches (the reviewer used the cargo registry sources under the cargo home and a home-like fixture; a test needs its own small tree where, say, `benchmrak` has an accidental in-order match in some long path and `benchmark.rs` exists). Then change what decides that near misses are not wanted. A starting point: near misses are left out only when the search has a match that has every checked word in one place, that is, as a run of letters in the path inside the folder searched (`hit.rel` contains the word), which is what a correctly spelled word gives. When no hit has that, and Allow typos is on, keep what the fallback keeps today (each checked word in order along the path, or a near miss of it within its budget, or `may_be_spelled_apart`) in addition to the in-order matches, so that the manual's scattered matches (`taxexemptionc` finding `tax/exemption/coding/Handler.java`, initials such as `tec` finding TaxExemptionController.java, whose budget is 0 anyway) stay, and the file that was meant is listed with them. Then rank: a near miss of a word in the file's name must come ahead of matches whose letters are only scattered along the path, and ahead of a near miss in a folder's name; `rerank` gives its name bonuses only to words found as typed, so a near miss in the name needs one of its own, smaller than a real match's. Check the other direction as carefully: a correctly spelled word must list exactly what it lists today (`man` must not start listing `main`; the reviewer's model checked 11,976 searches old against new, see their notes for how), and Allow typos off must list exactly what it lists today. `strict_words` and `changes_for` (which decide whether a new file is a live search's business) pass over near misses today and the manual says so; keep that or make them follow, and say which. Apps (`app_hits`): give them the same near-miss rule only if it is small; else leave it and say so. Measure the cost: `near_miss` will now run for every search that has no match in one place, not only for searches that match nothing; the reviewer's figures for the fallback are in their record under Cost.
original_test_plan: Engine tests that fail today: in a tree where a misspelled word has an accidental in-order match, the search lists the file that was meant (one typo in a name), ahead of the accidental matches; the same for a transposition, a missing letter and an extra letter; a near miss in a file's name ranks ahead of a near miss in a folder's name (`mian`: main.rs before the files of a folder named Many). Guards that must hold before and after: a correctly spelled word lists the same hits in the same order as on the trunk (take a set of searches over a fixture and compare whole lists); with Allow typos off nothing changes; words of three letters or fewer never bring near misses; the manual's `taxexemptionc` example still lists its three names (engine::tests::quoted_words_match_names_letter_for_letter pins them). Say what the search costs before and after on a large tree.
original_risks: This is the default search path: a mistake changes what every search lists. The danger on one side is junk (near misses of correctly typed words, or of abbreviations), on the other a slower first letter (the heaviest search). The pool fff-search hands over is cut before these checks ('result-tie-break' explains `TIES_AHEAD` and `through_ties`): a near miss that is not in the pool cannot be listed, so say how often the meant file is in the pool at all in your fixture. 'live-search-results' reruns a search when `changes_for` says a new file is its business, and compares lists; if near misses now appear in lists that `changes_for` does not know about, a quiet rerun may or may not pick up a new near miss: say what happens.

verifier.claim_check: Not checked by a second reviewer. The reviewer of 'typo-fallback-near-miss' measured it on two trees and the orchestrator read the branch in `Engine::search` on the trunk (5624239): the near-miss fallback runs only when `raw.iter().any(&strict)` is false. Reproduce before changing anything; if you cannot build a tree where it happens, write the closed record with what you tried and return skipped.
verifier.implementation_notes: See the proposal: a starting point, not a checked plan. Read the done records of 'typo-fallback-near-miss' and 'result-tie-break' first; both describe this function in detail and list fixtures sized against its constants.

orchestrator_notes: 'typo-fallback-near-miss' (5624239) is on the trunk and wrote `near_miss`, `typo_budget`, `checked_words` and `may_be_spelled_apart`; 'accented-names-search' (queued) will replace `may_be_spelled_apart` by normalizing names and words, so leave that function's rule as it is. The manual's Allow typos row and its Ranking and limits paragraph describe today's rule exactly; rewrite what your change makes untrue.
